item.title: The Art World's Epstein Problem
item.description: How to root out corruption and depravity in our community, artists against ICE, the Washington Post lays off its art critic, the pitfalls of archival art, and more.

item.title: The Political Power of Glitter
item.description: Damien Davis on the loss of an artist's archive, glitter's defiance, Mona Lisa in the Epstein files, and more.

item.title: Interdisciplinary Graduate Programs at SFU’s School for the Contemporary Arts
item.description: Transform your art practice with access to internationally-recognized faculty and state-of-the-art facilities in downtown Vancouver. MFA and MA applications are accepted through February 15.

item.title: Spain’s Cosmic Mother of Modernism
item.description: Maruja Mallo viewed herself as an extension of her modernist paintings, in which female energy is a conduit for natural and even otherworldly forces.

item.title: Matthew Bogdanos Awarded Marica Vilcek Prize in Art History for Repatriation of Stolen Artifacts
item.description: The leader of the Manhattan DA’s Antiquities Trafficking Unit is acknowledged for his lifelong dedication to recovering and safeguarding looted antiquities.

item.title: Israel's Plan to Artwash Genocide at the Venice Biennale
item.description: The artwork at the heart of the pavilion promises to continue the project of denying Palestinian existence.

item.title: Art Books That Serve Up Beauty and Depth
item.description: Our favorite art books for February, the writings of Claude Cahun, and an imaginative history of Michelangelo and Titian.

item.title: How Liminalism Became the Defining Aesthetic of Our Time
item.description: This crowd-curated digital movement is one of the most pertinent and explicit reactions to our particular slice of dystopian late capitalism.

item.title: Five Shows to See in New York City Right Now
item.description: Three millennia of storytelling at the Morgan, Goya’s visions of war, Alison Nguyen’s diasporic tale, and Indigenous artistry in every medium imaginable.

item.title: Bad Bunny’s “Benito Bowl” Enters the Meme Canon
item.description: The half-time show tribute to Boricua and Latine pride was rife with cultural and political symbolism that resonated with millions.
